shared_elements: grid/columns of square glyph blocks with rounded corners
low-relief carved signs containing internal face-like and dotted details
vertical, tall rectangular field organized in registers
paired columns of repeated sign-cartouches read as a sequence
justification: Both surfaces carry the same distinctive convention of square-with-rounded-corner sign cartouches, filled with compact face-like and dotted infill, set in double columns to be read in sequence down a tall vertical field — a specific correspondence unlikely to arise independently. The decisive difference is that A is dominated by an elaborately costumed standing human figure with a large plumed headdress standing on a basal register, with the glyph columns as a subordinate side panel, whereas B depicts nothing but the glyph grid, so the figure–text relationship central to A is absent.
